condition.semantics_statement: `condition` names the patient POPULATION the paper studied. A collagen-biology paper with no EDS/HSD cohort is `general` even if it informs EDS; a paper that carries an EDS/HSD label without studying that population is a bucket violation, recorded in the additive annotations table and never corrected in place.
condition.definitions_version: eds dry-run v1 (2026-09-30); EDS_hypermobility inherited from CONDITION_BUCKET_DEFINITIONS.md v1 and split

enum.definition: Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome as the studied population: cohorts diagnosed under the 2017 hEDS criteria, and pre-2017 cohorts the paper labels "EDS hypermobility type" / "EDS type III". Includes hEDS comorbid with POTS, MCAS or GI dysmotility when hEDS is the specific subject. Nearest exclusions: hypermobility spectrum disorder goes to `HSD`; a cohort pooling hEDS and HSD without separate reporting goes to `multiple`; "joint hypermobility syndrome" cohorts without an EDS label go to `hypermobility_unspecified`.

Hypermobility spectrum disorder (generalized, historical, localized or peripheral HSD, 2017 framework) as the studied population. Nearest exclusions: hEDS goes to `hEDS`; a pooled "hEDS/HSD" cohort goes to `multiple`; Beighton-assessed hypermobility without an HSD diagnosis goes to `hypermobility_unspecified`.

Any 2017-classification EDS type OTHER than hypermobile, as the studied population, with the type named in `eds_type`: classical (cEDS), classical-like (clEDS), cardiac-valvular (cvEDS), vascular (vEDS), arthrochalasia (aEDS), dermatosparaxis (dEDS), kyphoscoliotic (kEDS), brittle cornea syndrome (BCS), spondylodysplastic (spEDS), musculocontractural (mcEDS), myopathic (mEDS), periodontal (pEDS), or a newer molecularly defined type. Includes single-family and case reports of a named type. Nearest exclusions: hypermobile EDS goes to `hEDS`; a cohort of mixed or unstated EDS type goes to `EDS_unspecified_or_mixed`.

An Ehlers-Danlos cohort whose type is not stated, or that pools several EDS types without reporting them separately (e.g. registry, survey or claims-code "EDS" cohorts). Nearest exclusions: a single named type goes to `hEDS` or `EDS_other_type`; a cohort that ALSO includes HSD or GJH as a separately described group goes to `multiple`.

Generalized or joint hypermobility assessed by Beighton score or an equivalent instrument WITHOUT an EDS or HSD diagnosis, including pre-2017 "joint hypermobility syndrome" (JHS/BJHS) cohorts not labelled EDS, and hypermobility studied as a trait in athletes, dancers or general-population samples. Inherited from CONDITION_BUCKET_DEFINITIONS.md v1 (EDS_hypermobility: "generalized joint hypermobility assessed by Beighton score WITHOUT an EDS diagnosis"). Nearest exclusion: orthopaedic single-joint laxity/instability with no hypermobility-as-condition question is `general` (and usually topical drift).
Several listed conditions are subjects of the paper and reported as distinct groups — the typical case is a pooled or side-by-side hEDS and HSD cohort, or an EDS-types comparison that includes hEDS.

The correct answer when no listed condition is the paper's subject: connective-tissue or collagen biology without an EDS/HSD cohort, other heritable connective-tissue disorders (Marfan, Loeys-Dietz, osteogenesis imperfecta) studied alone, and comparison groups. A catch-all by design; "too vague" is not a defect.

scope.topical_drift: orthopaedic and sports-medicine single-joint laxity/instability papers (shoulder, patellar, ankle, TMJ) with no hypermobility-as-condition question; dental/periodontal papers that mention EDS only in a differential list; materials-science papers using EDS for spectroscopy; sleep-medicine papers using EDS for excessive daytime sleepiness
